title: Z.ai GLM 4.6: What We Learned From 100 Million Open Source Downloads — Yuxuan Zhang, Z.ai

primary.label: Model Foundations & Behavior
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 52%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary object is the GLM 4.6 foundation model itself, covering architecture, pretraining data, RL training dynamics, and intrinsic capabilities. The GLM family serves general-purpose LLM use cases and includes a coding plan integrating with developer tools. The talk covers pretraining with 15T tokens, post-training RL via SLIME, evaluation on benchmarks like CC-bench, and deployment via vLLM and SGLang. Content assumes familiarity with RL for LLMs, pretraining pipelines, and deployment frameworks. A conference-style technical presentation with slides, benchmark results, and demo videos. Multiple specific quantitative claims and training details are directly grounded in transcript evidence.

summary: Z.ai has been committed to open source since 2022, releasing over 65 models across language (GLM), multimodal understanding (GLM-V/CogVLM), image generation, and video generation. GLM 4.6 is their latest flagship, tying for #1 on LMSYS Chatbot Arena with GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet as the only open-source model at that rank. They also built CC-bench v1.1, an agent-style coding benchmark with 74 tasks, where GLM 4.6 achieves ~68.6% win rate against Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4. The training pipeline starts with 15T tokens of general pre-training data at 4K context, followed by 7T tokens of reasoning and code data, mid-training with repo-level code contexts at 32K, 500B tokens of synthetic reasoning data, and 100B tokens of long-context agent data extending to 200K tokens. SLIME is their open-source RL framework supporting both synchronous mode (for short reasoning tasks, training and inference on the same GPU) and asynchronous mode (for complex agent tasks with external environments). Key RL lessons include a two-stage difficulty curriculum, single-stage RL at 64K tokens to preserve long-context ability, token-weighted loss for coding to avoid short template answers, and prioritizing data quality over quantity for scientific reasoning. GLM 4.5V supports image and video understanding with native resolution processing, time-index tokens for video, and GUI agent capabilities via CogAgent. GLM 4.6 has over 355 billion parameters, requiring significant GPU resources for local deployment. Models are deployable through vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face, and frameworks like LLaMA Factory and MS-Swift. Z.AI also provides a web platform and API, plus a GLM coding plan connecting the model with coding tools. The team regularly hosts community events including Reddit AMAs and offline tech sharing sessions.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction & The GLM Ecosystem
sections.summary: Z.ai has been committed to open source since 2022, releasing 65+ models across language, multimodal, image, and video domains. In 2025 they released GLM-4 0414 dense models and GLM-4.5/4.6 MoE series. The ecosystem has surpassed 100 million downloads with 105,500 community projects on GitHub.

sections.title: GLM 4.6 Benchmark Performance & CC-bench
sections.summary: GLM 4.6 shows gains over GLM 4.5 on math and coding benchmarks, beats Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4 on several benchmarks, and ties for #1 on LMSYS Chatbot Arena with GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet as the only open-source model. CC-bench v1.1 provides 74 agent coding tasks where GLM 4.6 achieves ~68.6% win rate against Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4.

sections.title: Training Pipeline: Pre-training to Long Context
sections.summary: The pipeline starts with 15T tokens of general pre-training at 4K context, then 7T tokens of reasoning/code data, mid-training with repo-level code at 32K context, 500B tokens of synthetic reasoning data, and 100B tokens of long-context agent data extending to 200K tokens. Repo-level training packs multiple files, issues, and pull requests into one long context.

sections.title: SLIME: Efficient RL Framework for Agents
sections.summary: SLIME is Z.ai's open-source RL framework using Megatron for training and a high-throughput inference coaster. It supports synchronous mode (same GPU for training and inference, best for short reasoning) and asynchronous decoupled mode (for complex agent tasks with external environments). Slow tasks don't block the pipeline. Efficiency optimizations include BF16 training with blockwise FP16 weight synchronization.

sections.title: RL Lessons: Curriculum, Single-Stage, Token-Weighted Loss
sections.summary: A two-stage difficulty curriculum uses medium problems first then hard problems. Single-stage RL at 64K tokens outperforms multi-stage RL because shorter stages cause long-context forgetting. Token-weighted loss for coding converges faster and reduces short template answer gaming. For scientific reasoning, small high-quality datasets outperform large mixed-quality ones.

sections.title: GLM 4.5V: Multimodal & Video Understanding
sections.summary: GLM 4.5V supports image and video understanding with native resolution processing, avoiding fixed-square cropping. Time-index tokens inserted after each video frame help temporal understanding. CogAgent-based GUI agent capability supports computer and browser control.

sections.title: Deployment, Coding Assistants & Community
sections.summary: GLM 4.6 has over 355 billion parameters, requiring approximately 100+ GPUs for local deployment. Models are accessible via vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face, LLaMA Factory, and MS-Swift, or through Z.AI's web platform and API which supports Google search, code generation, and PowerPoint creation. The GLM coding plan integrates the model with coding tools and plugins. A demo video shows replacing a coding assistant model with GLM 4.6. Z.AI hosts regular community events including Reddit AMAs and offline tech sharing sessions, with Discord and GitHub links for engagement.
